NEITHER ROUND IS REVERSED: both fixed real defects that still stand; both cards were already sitting on the FLOOR of their bands (60 and 64) with zero room down before this round, because both are assisted-diet bigs, and the discount takes each one point lower. A later round that wants those pins back has to say which of the two rulings stands.

82, NOT 78 — HE CONFIRMED 82, AND WHY 78 IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THIS TERM. The subject's PRE-SMOOTH bar goes 79 -> 75. The 20/60/20 season blend then averages him with his own '03 (pre-smooth 98 -> 91) and '05 (93 -> 86), which are the SAME assisted shape and carry 40% of the card, so the stored bar reads 82. Deleting the premium outright reaches 79 but costs 8 anchors and drops Shaq '00-'02 to rim 97 and Zion '24 to 81; cutting only the neighbours is a per-card use of the smoother, which doctrine 1 forbids. 78 needs a ruling on the smoother, not on this term.

THE ONE RISE ON THE BOARD IS NOT THIS TERM'S — IT IS is_big's CLIFF IN compute_ovr.py, AND IT IS OUT OF LANE. Nothing rises on any ATTRIBUTE (2,003 rim bars fall, 0 rise). But THREE cards cross is_big's middle shape clause `rim >= 60 and 3pt < 40` on the way down and are re-graded on the perimeter vector: Larry Johnson '99 (rim 60 -> 59) OFF 51 -> 55 and OVR 51 -> 54, Metta World Peace '04 (60 -> 57) OFF 67 -> 66, Jaime Jaquez Jr. '26 (62 -> 56) OFF 58 -> 57. Only Johnson rises, by 4 on OFF, on a ONE-POINT fall in rim. compute_ovr.py's own comment at line 130 already names this clause "THE DEFECT"; a one-point attribute step should not be worth four points of OFF and this round is the second time it has fired on a rim change. It belongs to ratings-to-off-def.

ONE TEST FAILS AND IT IS OUT OF MY LANE — tests/court.test.ts "a man who cannot shoot is never sent out to space the floor > holds in every shape, called or inferred" (410 of 411 pass; the pre-round tree was 411/411 green). CAUSE, exactly: Deandre Ayton '26 is an assisted-diet big and his rim goes 71 -> 68, so screenFit = min(max(rim, mid), efficiency) = min(70, 81) = 70 where it was min(71, 81) = 71. Rui Hachimura '26 reads 71, capped by his efficiency 71. They were TIED at 71 and pnrPair broke the tie by the roll (rim 71 to 27) in Ayton's favour — that tie-break is written into src/engine/tactics.ts line 742 and quoted in the test's own recal_120 comment. At 70 vs 71 it is no longer a tie, Hachimura takes the screen, and the pick-and-roll set stands AYTON (3pt 4) IN A CORNER, which is the ruling the test guards. THIS IS EXACTLY THE COLLATERAL recal_145 REFUSED TO PAY and named by card ('the two cards it moves by a single point are Deandre Ayton '26 ... those two points re-decide a screen tie-break ... pinned in tests/court.test.ts'). The difference is that this time the rim move is Tomer's own confirmed ruling, so the bar is right and the FLOOR is wrong: the real defect is that the pnr set corners the non-screener big at all, whatever his three. THE FIX IS NOT AN ATTRIBUTE and this agent owns only data/build_ratings.py — it belongs either in src/ui/CourtFive.tsx (never put a man with canSpace false on a corner spot; the inside/dunker spot is free in the pnr set) or in src/engine/tactics.ts's pnrPair (break a NEAR-tie on screenFit by the roll, not an exact one). Nothing in data/ can reach it without a per-player override. Flagged for the engine/ui round; every anchor, every receipt and the other 410 tests pass.

THE SUBJECT, TERM BY TERM. data/provenance.json rim [1, 8.61, 0.532, 0.726]: 8.61 paint attempts per 100 (0-10 ft), 53.2% conversion — the 57th percentile of 2004 — and 72.6% of his 2P makes assisted, on BPM -2.8 and 14.7 ppg. creation_factor = 1 - 0.45 x 0.726 = 0.673, so the composite reads P_rimvol(5.79) = 0.813 at weight 0.65. The premium read P_rimvol(8.61) = 0.991 and paid 0.07 x (0.991 - 0.70)/0.30 = +0.0679, seven card points, for volume the composite had already said he did not create. It now pays 0.07 x (0.813 - 0.70)/0.30 = +0.0263. Pre-smooth 79 -> 75; smoothed 86 -> 82.

THE POOL STAYS RAW ON PURPOSE and it is why the mid-class bigs fall hardest. vol_rim collects undiscounted volumes ('adjusted value ranks as self-created-equivalent volume'), so a discounted reading moves an assisted big down the WHOLE class rather than past only the cards more assisted than he is. That is the shape recal_51 built and this round did not re-open it: the gate (0.70), the payment (0.07) and the band (0.30) are all byte-identical.

REJECTED, each measured on the full 10,000-card pool before landing: (1) scaling the discount by t in [0,1] — t <= 0.10 holds the OLD pins and moves the subject by ZERO, t = 0.15 already takes Nene out, so there was no partial form to hide behind and the choice was genuinely release-the-pins or decline; (2) ranking the discounted value against a DISCOUNTED pool — the subject keeps 0.0615 of 0.0679, six tenths of a card point; (3) deleting the premium — the subject reaches 79 but 8 anchors fail and Shaq '00-'02 fall to rim 97 with Zion '24 to 81, which is the volume-first doctrine itself. Round 166 was DECLINED on this measurement first; Tomer read the frontier and released the two pins.
